subChunks.title: Spring Boot Auto-Configuration & Starters

storyBeats.text: Where Spring Framework hands you a blank spellbook, Spring Boot hands you one already filled with the most-used incantations — ready to override or extend.

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: Auto-configuration is not magic — it's convention. Spring sees jackson-databind on the classpath and configures an ObjectMapper for you. Add your own @Bean and Spring steps aside.

guidedPractice.problemHtml: List the three meta-annotations that @SpringBootApplication combines. Print each on a separate line.

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain Spring Boot auto-configuration. How does Spring decide whether to apply an auto-configuration class?

questions.explanation: @SpringBootApplication is a composed annotation that enables component scanning, configuration, and auto-configuration in one.

questions.prompt: Spring Boot auto-configuration can be overridden by providing your own @Bean.
questions.explanation: Spring Boot uses @ConditionalOnMissingBean — if you define a bean of the same type, Spring Boot's auto-configured one backs off.

subChunks.title: Application Properties & Profiles

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: Profiles are the Academy's environmental seals. The same spell behaves differently in the training grounds vs. the field. Never hard-code environment-specific values — use application.yml.

guidedPractice.problemHtml: Simulate profile-aware configuration: if a String profile is "prod", print the prod DB URL; otherwise print the dev URL.

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain Spring profiles. How would you configure different database URLs for dev and prod?

questions.prompt: How do you activate a Spring profile at startup?
options: --spring.profiles.active=prod JVM argument or SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE env var
questions.answer: --spring.profiles.active=prod JVM argument or SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE env var
questions.explanation: Profiles are activated via JVM args, environment variables, or application.yml's spring.profiles.active.

subChunks.title: Actuator & Observability

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: Actuator is your crystal ball for production systems. Load balancers ping /actuator/health every 30 seconds. If it returns DOWN, traffic stops routing to that instance automatically.

guidedPractice.problemHtml: Simulate a health check: create a HealthChecker with a boolean dbReachable field. If reachable, print UP; otherwise print DOWN: database unreachable.

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: What Actuator endpoints would you expose in production? Which would you restrict and why?

questions.prompt: Which Actuator endpoint do load balancers typically use?
questions.explanation: Health is the standard liveness/readiness endpoint. Load balancers route traffic away from DOWN instances.

subChunks.title: Build, Testing & Deployment

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: The fat JAR is your sealed spell tome — everything needed to cast the spell, contained in one artefact. Ship that JAR anywhere Java runs and the application comes alive.

guidedPractice.problemHtml: Write a method buildCommand(String profile) that returns the correct java -jar command string for a given profile.

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain the difference between @WebMvcTest, @DataJpaTest, and @SpringBootTest. When would you use each?

questions.prompt: What is a 'fat JAR' in Spring Boot?
options: An executable JAR containing the app and all its dependencies including an embedded server
A JAR with only source files
A compressed ZIP of the project
A WAR file deployed to a separate Tomcat
questions.answer: An executable JAR containing the app and all its dependencies including an embedded server
questions.explanation: Spring Boot packages everything — including Tomcat — into one runnable JAR. No external server required.
